Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/infiniband/hw/mlx5/main.c`**
   - The order of operations in the `mlx5_ib_unbind_slave_port` function has been modified.
   - The spinlock (`mpi_lock`) is now released before unregistering the notifier (`mlx5_notifier_unregister`).
   - The lines that unregister the notifier and set `mpi->mdev_events.notifier_call` to `NULL` have been moved below the spinlock release, ensuring that the notifier is unregistered only after the lock is released.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The primary relationship between the modifications is that they address a kernel panic issue caused by holding a spinlock while attempting to unregister a notifier. By releasing the spinlock before the unregister operation, the patch prevents the "scheduling while atomic" bug, allowing the system to handle scheduling properly without being blocked by the spinlock. This change improves the stability of the system when using bond mode LACP with GRE tunnels.

Fixes: df097a278c75 ("IB/mlx5: Use the new mlx5 core notifier API")
Signed-off-by: Leon Romanovsky <leonro@mellanox.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20190731083852.584-1-leon@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Doug Ledford <dledford@redhat.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by not releasing the spinlock during the notifier unregister sequence in the `mlx5_ib_unbind_slave_port` function. This led to a situation where the system attempted to schedule while holding the spinlock, resulting in a kernel panic due to preemption being disabled.

Here is the patch:
 /* The mlx5_ib_multiport_mutex should be held when calling this function */
 static void mlx5_ib_unbind_slave_port(struct mlx5_ib_dev *ibdev,
 				      struct mlx5_ib_multiport_info *mpi)
 {
 	u8 port_num = mlx5_core_native_port_num(mpi->mdev) - 1;
 	struct mlx5_ib_port *port = &ibdev->port[port_num];
 	int comps;
 	int err;
 	int i;
 
 	mlx5_ib_cleanup_cong_debugfs(ibdev, port_num);
 
 	spin_lock(&port->mp.mpi_lock);
 	if (!mpi->ibdev) {
 		spin_unlock(&port->mp.mpi_lock);
 		return;
 	}
 
-	if (mpi->mdev_events.notifier_call)
-		mlx5_notifier_unregister(mpi->mdev, &mpi->mdev_events);
-	mpi->mdev_events.notifier_call = NULL;
-
 	mpi->ibdev = NULL;
 
 	spin_unlock(&port->mp.mpi_lock);
+	if (mpi->mdev_events.notifier_call)
+		mlx5_notifier_unregister(mpi->mdev, &mpi->mdev_events);
+	mpi->mdev_events.notifier_call = NULL;
 	mlx5_remove_netdev_notifier(ibdev, port_num);
 	spin_lock(&port->mp.mpi_lock);
 
 	comps = mpi->mdev_refcnt;
 	if (comps) {
 		mpi->unaffiliate = true;
 		init_completion(&mpi->unref_comp);
 		spin_unlock(&port->mp.mpi_lock);
 
 		for (i = 0; i < comps; i++)
 			wait_for_completion(&mpi->unref_comp);
 
 		spin_lock(&port->mp.mpi_lock);
 		mpi->unaffiliate = false;
 	}
 
 	port->mp.mpi = NULL;
 
 	list_add_tail(&mpi->list, &mlx5_ib_unaffiliated_port_list);
 
 	spin_unlock(&port->mp.mpi_lock);
 
 	err = mlx5_nic_vport_unaffiliate_multiport(mpi->mdev);
 
 	mlx5_ib_dbg(ibdev, "unaffiliated port %d\n", port_num + 1);
 	/* Log an error, still needed to cleanup the pointers and add
 	 * it back to the list.
 	 */
 	if (err)
 		mlx5_ib_err(ibdev, "Failed to unaffiliate port %u\n",
 			    port_num + 1);
 
 	ibdev->port[port_num].roce.last_port_state = IB_PORT_DOWN;
 }
